name: Vodka Sauce
author: Dan Pelosi
description: This vodka sauce recipe, adapted from my cookbook “Let’s Eat” (Union Square & Co., 2023), leans into the creamier, glossier side of this traditional Italian sauce. It avoids using alliums like shallot or onion or salty meats like bacon or pancetta at the start of the recipe, instead focusing on whisking up a smooth sauce that highlights the famously sweet and tangy flavor that results from cooking the alcohol out of the vodka. While most traditionally used on pasta, this sauce also brings new life to chicken Parmesan or pizza. It is easily made vegan with the use of non-dairy cream substitutes, and comes back to life as leftovers by adding just a splash or two of pasta water while reheating.

ingredients.raw: Freshly grated Parmesan or pecorino cheese, for serving
ingredients.item: freshly grated parmesan or pecorino cheese

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.

Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium heat, combine the olive oil, butter and a pinch of crushed red pepper (if using). Cook, whisking to blend the fats together while the butter is melting. Add the garlic and tomato paste. Whisk until the tomato paste is deep red, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add the rigatoni to the boiling water and cook until al dente according to the package directions. Reserve 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain and set aside.

As soon as the pasta hits the water, add the heavy cream to the skillet and continue whisking until the cream is fully incorporated and the sauce color darkens slightly, about 5 minutes. Add the vodka to the sauce and cook, continuing to whisk, until the alcohol cooks out (the strong scent of the vodka will disappear), and the sauce is perfectly smooth, about 5 minutes more.
Add ½ cup of the reserved pasta water to the sauce. Continue to simmer and whisk frequently until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon without sliding off, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the cooked pasta to the sauce and stir until coated and glossy. Divide among plates, top with Parmesan, and serve.
